claim: Free-choice any, unlike non-affirmative any, permits modification, for example by almost.
evidence_summary: §11(b), p. 431: “The approximate negators hardly, barely, scarcely can modify anyn”. Page 424 [45iia] has They did [hardly any] work. Page 816 makes the same point.
finding: The contrast holds for almost-type approximators. Non-affirmative any takes the approximate negators. Brett’s determinatives paper relies on the p. 431 description.
proposed_wording: Anyf, unlike anyn, permits modification by almost, nearly or practically. Anyn takes only the approximate negators hardly, barely and scarcely (§11).
inference: Does the almost contrast show that only free-choice any can be modified?

evidence.passage: §7.5, p. 383 [36]. “anyf, unlike anyn, permits modification, for example by the adverb almost.”
evidence.example: §11(b), p. 431, and p. 424 [45iia] They did [hardly any] work.
evidence.establishes: A direct conflict between two descriptions of the same determinative.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
